newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PARTY STILL MULLING CABINET REPLACEMENT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PARTY STILL MULLING CABINET REPLACEMENT.

text.p: Leaders of a junior party in the Czech ruling coalition, the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA), are to meet on Sunday to discuss further steps after the shock resignation of deputy premier and justice minister Jan Kalvoda.

Party spokesman David Rozanek on Thursday said Deputy Chairman Karel Ledvinka would represent the ODA in coalition talks on replacing Kalvoda, the chairman of ODA who quit the cabinet and parliament on Tuesday after admitting to using an unattained "Doctor of Law" title.
Party officials said they have four candidates to take over Kalvoda's seat as justice minister, but did not reveal any names.
Rozanek told Reuters that he did not expect a final candidate to be nominated on Sunday when the party's second-level organ, the "central assembly" meets on Sunday.

The pro-business ODA is entitled to four seats in the 16-member cabinet under a coalition agreement with the centre-right Civic Democratic Party (ODS) of Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, and the centrist Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL).
The ODA's smallest executive body, the executive council, has asked Kalvoda to remain as leader of the party until their national congress, due to be held in March.
President Vaclav Havel has asked him to reconsider his decision to quit. Kalvoda has not given any concrete response to either offer.
"We will have a meeting on the current situation. Maybe the participants of (Sunday's) central assembly meeting will call the party conference for earlier than March," Rozanek said.
Kalvoda, a cabinet member since 1992, was the fifth member of parliament who admitted using unattained title of Juris Doctor in an affair which shocked the country.
Out of the other four fake doctors, only one has resigned her parliamentary seat.
